text:
maria-ops: Heads up, we're getting a lot of GPU job failures when spot nodes get interruption notices this week (batch jobs + long fine-tunes). ~30% fail/retry during day.
jonathan: ugh. are those failures because pods get killed mid-checkpoint or because CA deletes nodes before pods reschedule?
maria-ops: mostly killed mid-checkpoint. preStop hooks don't always finish, and some jobs don't tolerate SIGTERM long enough.
ali: two quick wins: (1) add a short-lived on-demand "surge" nodegroup sized for your peak concurrent GPU jobs, and (2) run a termination-handler DaemonSet that cordons + drains with a configurable grace window.
samir: +1. we used a tiny on-demand pool (1-2 gpus each) as a buffer and the CA expander set to prefer the cheaper pools but keep one on-demand around.
jonathan: also send termination notices to a controller that can trigger job-level checkpoints. we wired ours to an S3 checkpoint step in preStop.
ali: example preStop snippet we use in our training job containers:
```
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "python /app/save_checkpoint.py --dest s3://redwood-checkpoints/$JOB_ID || true"]
```
maria-ops: nice. any cluster-autoscaler tweaks recommended for mixed GPU pools?
samir: we've got this set for GPU stacks:
```
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
--expander=least-waste
--max-empty-bulk-delete=6
--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
--scale-down-unneeded-time=12m
--scale-down-unready-time=8m
```
samir: the key is to tune scale-down delays so CA doesn't immediately rip out the surge nodes while termination handler still draining.
jonathan: also taint the spot pool with `spot=true:NoSchedule` and give long-running training pods a toleration only when they request the spot class. That way best-effort jobs go to spot, critical ones prefer on-demand.
ali: another tactic: when a termination notice arrives, the handler can call the webhook to the scheduler to migrate pods by creating an eviction with a longer gracePeriodSeconds. Something like:
```
kubectl evict --force --grace-period=90 pod/<name>
```
jonathan: infra-bot showed we get ~2 minutes notice on AWS spot and ~30s on GCE preemptible — so tune grace windows per cloud.
infra-bot: k8s event: Node ip-10-0-45-12.ec2.internal received SpotInterruptionNotice, 120s remaining (handled by termination-handler v2.1)
maria-ops: good to know. what about cost tradeoffs? the surge group adds cost but reduces retries.
samir: calculate break-even: cost_of_retries = (avg_job_time * retry_rate * vGPU_cost) vs surge_hour_cost. in our case keeping a 2-node on-demand buffer saved ~18% infra spend because jobs finished rather than being restarted.
ali: also consider checkpoint frequency: more frequent small checkpoints reduce lost work when a spot node dies.
jonathan: last tip: expose metrics from termination-handler and checkpoint duration to Grafana so SRE can set alerts for increasing failure rates.
maria-ops: sweet. I'll spin up a 2-node on-demand surge group, deploy the handler, and add the preStop. will report back tomorrow. :thumbsup:
jonathan: thanks, excited to see the numbers.
ali: ping me if you want help with the checkpoint script.

maria-ops: noted, thanks all.
